Synopsis:
Rising Treasury yields are partly driven by upward pressure on R-star (the neutral/natural rate), estimated at 1.65% by the NY Fed's Laubach-Williams model but likely higher in practice. The culprits are AI-driven capital spending by hyperscalers and surging government borrowing (national debt at $40T), both competing for capital and lifting real yields structurally. This "higher-for-longer" dynamic complicates Fed rate cuts across the entire yield curve, with the 30-year most affected due to fiscal deficits and long-term bond supply. A minority view holds that AI could eventually prove disinflationary, temporarily reversing the R-star rise, but analysts broadly agree it is too early to distinguish a structural shift from a cyclical phenomenon.
